subject: cyborgMedic
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: support-hero cyborg medic with a healing staff.
Style: Overwatch.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I'm spotting a few issues: the cuirass chest piece reads as a shaggy white blob with a jagged top that clips oddly against the neck, giving it a bulbous look, and the hair seems to clip strangely too. I also notice the wings don't look right—only one appears visible in the three-quarter view.

Checking other details: the backpack in side view looks fine as a gray box, the staff and arm placement seem okay, but the legs look stilt-like with thin lower shins and mottled steel paint, plus the proportions overall skew more realistic than the chunky, stylized Overwatch look. Given limited edit effort, I'm weighing whether scaling the head up is worth it since it touches too many parts, so I'm focusing instead on smaller fixable issues like hand and arm positioning.

Looking closer, I notice jagged white fringe at the neck where the cuirass top meets the collar — it seems the collar cylinder is getting hidden under the cuirass's rounded cap and the suit's top station poking through. To fix this I'm planning to lower and narrow the cuirass's final station, enlarge and raise the collar cylinder's dimensions, and adjust the suit's top station so the neck reads cleanly without z-fighting.

The wings also look a bit flat and asymmetric in three-quarter view, so I'm considering adding a thin extra feather layer for detail, though it's a minor fix. Everything else — the glow, face features, eye placement, staff orb, and base tiles — looks acceptable as is, though the base hex reads a bit dark.

The legs are bothering me more: the lower legs look thin compared to the bulky torso, so I want to bump up the shin radii slightly. I'm also noticing both lower legs appear grey and mottled in the front view, which suggests the STEEL metal paint is bleeding onto both sides instead of the SUIT material showing correctly on one leg — I need to check the sweep ranges controlling which paint applies where.

The grey mottling on armor is actually coming from the ground-darkening effect combined with noise tint, making it look dirty rather than intentional shading. I should reduce the ground darkening threshold and noise intensity for the ARMOR material to clean it up — a cheap but effective fix. Hands, hair, jaw, and chest gradient all look fine as-is, and the tabard and drone placement don't need changes either.

For the wings, instead of adding glowing edge rods, I'll add a couple of slimmer feather extrudes at a different rotation angle with a lighter teal tint for extra depth, keeping it simple.

Writing the ARMOR color blend edit...

Then I'm adjusting the cuirass and suit end stations slightly to narrow the neck transition, tweaking positions and sizes so the collar geometry lines up cleanly, and reworking the collar cylinder and torus pieces for a tighter fit.

Next I'm adjusting the leg radius taper values to slim the lower legs, and considering adding an edit to the wing extrusion block to extend its shape parameters.

Then I'll insert a pale back feather layer behind the main wing extrude, slightly offset in z, so the wings read as bigger and more layered.
